dervis-irab:33-42.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حاصِباً): a wind that pelted them (ḥaṣabathum), i.e. pelted them with stones and pebbles (al-ḥaṣbāʾ). Al-Farazdaq said:
مستقبلين شمال الشام تضربنا ... بحاصب كنديف القطن منثور
(Facing the north wind of Syria, it strikes us with a pelting gust like scattered carded cotton.)
In al-Mukhtār: "al-ḥaṣbāʾ, with the long vowel, means pebbles; from it comes al-Muḥaṣṣab, a place in the Hijaz. Al-ḥāṣib is a violent wind that stirs up pebbles. Al-ḥaṣab, with two fatḥas, is that with which a fire is pelted (tuḥṣab), i.e. thrown into it; anything you throw into a fire, you have 'ḥaṣabta' the fire with it. Its pattern is that of ḍaraba." More on its meaning will come in the I'rab section.
(بِسَحَرٍ): saḥar, when indefinite, means one of the pre-dawn times; one says: "I saw Zayd at a pre-dawn (saḥaran), one of the pre-dawns." Had a particular day's saḥar been meant, it would have been a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), because it would then be definite and deflected (maʿdūl) from al-saḥar, since its proper form when definite is with al-. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "(بسحر): at a portion of the night, namely its last sixth. It is also said: there are two saḥars; the upper saḥar is before the breaking of dawn, and the other at its breaking. He recited:
يا سائلي إن كنت عنها تسأل ... مرّت بأعلى السحرين تذأل
(O you who ask me, if you are asking about her: she passed by at the upper of the two pre-dawns, trotting briskly.)
It is fully declined (munṣarif) because it is indefinite." Moreover, there is disagreement over the definiteness of the diptote form. It is said that it is a diptote because of definiteness and deflection ('adl). As for the definiteness, there is disagreement about it: it is said that it is definite as a proper name, because it has been made a name for this time; and it is said that it resembles a proper name, because it is definite without an overt marker, like a proper name. As for the deflection, its form is deflected from al-saḥar with al-, because when a specific one is meant, it should by origin be mentioned definite with al-; so the word with al- was abandoned while definiteness was still intended, and so it was made a diptote. Al-Suhaylī and al-Shalawbīn the Younger said it is definite [and] known, and they differed over the reason its nunation is withheld: al-Suhaylī said it is with an intended annexation (iḍāfa), and al-Shalawbīn said with an intended al-.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِالنُّذُرِ): a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بالنذر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كذبت).
(إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ حاصِباً إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ نَجَّيْناهُمْ بِسَحَرٍ): inna and its noun, and the clause (أرسلنا) is its khabar (predicate); (عليهم) is attached to (أرسلنا); (حاصبا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of exception; (آل لوط) is excepted by (إلا). In this exception there are two views. The first is that it is connected (muttaṣil), the meaning being that He sent the pelting wind upon all of them except his family, upon whom He did not send it. The second is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), the meaning being that He did not send it upon the family of Lot. The [correct] view is the first. (نجيناهم) is a verb and its agent, and (بسحر) is attached to (نجيناهم).
(نِعْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ): (نعمة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) agreeing with its governor in meaning, namely (نجيناهم), since rescuing is a favour; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) giving the reason for "anjaynāhum" — al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this and confined himself to it. [Translator's note: the source writes «أنجيناهم» here, while the verse has (نجيناهم).] (من عندنا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (نعمة). (كذلك) is attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted absolute object, i.e. "the like of that rescue". (نجزي) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (من) is a relative noun, direct object; and the clause (شكر) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلَقَدْ أَنْذَرَهُمْ بَطْشَتَنا فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُّذُرِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (أنذرهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a first direct object; (بطشتنا) is a second direct object, or it is accusative by removal of the preposition — two views. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (تماروا) is a past verb and the wāw is its agent, i.e. they pushed back the warning by way of disputation; (بالنذر) is attached to (تماروا).
(وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ): the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause; (عن ضيفه) is attached to (راودوه); (فطمسنا) is conjoined to (راودوه); (أعينهم) is a direct object. The fāʾ is conjunctive and what it conjoins is omitted, i.e. "so We said to them"; the clause (ذوقوا) is the speech quoted by the omitted verb of saying; (عذابي) is the object of (ذوقوا); (نذر) is conjoined to (عذابي), and the yāʾ of the first person has been dropped, as preceded.
(وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُمْ بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ): also conjoined. (بكرة) is an adverb of time attached to "ṣaḥabahum" [Translator's note: so in the source, «بصحبهم»; evidently a misprint for (صبّحهم)], i.e. not on a specific day; (عذاب) is the agent, and (مستقر) is an adjective of (عذاب), i.e. it will not depart from them.
(فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ): its i'rab has preceded.
(وَلَقَدْ جاءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ النُّذُرُ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded.
(كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كُلِّها فَأَخَذْناهُمْ أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ): resumptive speech, set forth to answer a question arising from the account of the warnings' coming, as though it were said: "So what did they do then?" and it was said: "They denied." (بآياتنا) is attached to (كذبوا), and (كلها) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of (آياتنا). (فأخذناهم): the fāʾ is conjunctive, and (أخذناهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (أخذ عزيز) is an absolute object, and (مقتدر) is an adjective of (عزيز); the annexation is that of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (al-takrīr): in the preceding verses there is a noticeable, deliberate repetition, whose purpose is reminding and rousing from the slumber of heedlessness that may come upon minds and veil them from reflection and contemplation, and cover them with the curtains of ignorance until they can scarcely see anything. More on this device will come in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.

dervis-irab:43-55.t:
* I'rab:
(أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أُولئِكُمْ أَمْ لَكُمْ بَراءَةٌ فِي الزُّبُرِ): (أكفاركم): the hamza is for the disapproving interrogative, which has the meaning of negation; (كفاركم) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (خير) is the khabar (predicate); (من أولئكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خير). (أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning "rather" (bal); it is for turning away (iḍrāb) and moving to another aspect of rebuke. (لكم) is a fronted predicate, (براءة) is a delayed subject, and (في الزبر) is a naʿt (adjective) of (براءة).
(أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ): what was said about (أم) has preceded. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (نحن) is a subject, (جميع) a predicate, and (منتصر) an adjective of (جميع), because it has the meaning of "a group" (jamʿ); the clause is the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl). (منتصر) was made singular only on account of the form of (جميع), which is singular in form even though it is a noun for a group, like "raht" (band) and "jaysh" (army). It is also said: it did not say "muntaṣirūn" in order to agree with the verse endings — and this is good.
(سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ): the sīn is a particle of the future; (يهزم) is an imperfect verb, passive; (الجمع) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (يولون) is conjoined to (سيهزم); and (الدبر) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It did not say "al-adbār" (backs), also to agree with the verse endings, and because it is a generic noun, since each one of them turns his back.
(بَلِ السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ وَالسَّاعَةُ أَدْهى وَأَمَرُّ): (بل) is a particle of turning away and conjunction; (الساعة) is a subject and (موعدهم) its predicate; the wāw is a conjunction; (الساعة) is a subject, (أدهى) its predicate, and (أمرّ) is conjoined to (الساعة) [Translator's note: so in the source; (أمرّ) is evidently conjoined to (أدهى)]. You may also make the wāw circumstantial (for the ḥāl).
(إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ): inna and its noun; (في ضلال) is its predicate.
(يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ): (يوم) is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "it will be said to them on the day they are dragged"; the clause (يسحبون) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (في النار) is attached to (يسحبون); (على وجوههم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (ذوقوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the speech quoted by the implied verb of saying. (مسّ) is a direct object and (سقر) a muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); it is a proper name for Hell, and that is why it is a diptote, since it is a feminine proper name.
(إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ): inna and its noun. (كل شيء) is accusative by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an omitted verb explained by what follows it, i.e. "We created everything; We created it"; the clause of the omitted verb is in the position of the nominative as the predicate of (إنّا), and the clause (خلقناه) is explicative, with no grammatical position. A long dispute has arisen over this verse, which we have summarised for you in the Benefits section. (بقدر) is attached to an omitted ḥāl of (كل), i.e. measured out, perfected and ordered.
(وَما أَمْرُنا إِلَّا واحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negating; (أمرنا) is a subject; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (واحدة) is the predicate of (أمرنا); (كلمح) is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the object of the command, namely the thing commanded into existence, i.e. in the state of its coming into being swiftly; (بالبصر) is attached to (لمح).
(وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا أَشْياعَكُمْ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded shortly before.
(وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِي الزُّبُرِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (كل) is a subject and (شيء) a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (فعلوه) is an adjective; (في الزبر) is the predicate, i.e. the books, plural of "zabūr".
(وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُسْتَطَرٌ): a subject and predicate, i.e. written down in the Preserved Tablet.
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ): inna and its noun; (في جنات) is its predicate; (نهر) is conjoined to (جنات).
(فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) of part for whole from His words (في جنات), because the seat is part of the gardens; or you may attach it to an omitted [word] as a second predicate of (إنّ). (عند مليك) is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of (جنات) or of (مقعد); it is also said to be a second or third predicate of (إنّ). (مليك) is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha).

* Benefits:
1- A dispute arose between Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila over the words of Allah the Exalted (إنّا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر). The rule laid down by the grammarians would call for the nominative of (كل), yet none of the Seven read it so, because with the nominative the speech is a single clause and with the accusative it is two clauses, so the nominative is more concise; moreover, there is nothing here requiring the accusative from any of the six categories, namely command, prohibition, interrogative, wish, hope and urging. Nor do we find here a fitting conjunction or anything else of the places they count as making the accusative preferable. Once this is clear, it is known that the nominative was abandoned by consensus only for a subtle secret that determines the choice of the accusative: had it been nominative, the clause (خلقناه) would fall as an adjective of (شيء), and (بقدر) would be raised as the predicate of "everything" restricted by the adjective, and the speech would amount to: "Indeed, everything created by Us is by measure." That would suggest that some created thing attributed to other than Allah the Exalted is not by measure. With the accusative, the speech becomes: "Indeed, We created everything by measure," which conveys the universality of the attribution of every created thing to Allah the Exalted. Since this benefit is not matched by the verbal benefit [of concision] in the nominative reading, together with the deficiency of meaning in the nominative, and with the meaning coming complete like the break of dawn in this widely transmitted reading, it is no wonder they agreed unanimously to abandon the nominative for the accusative.
However, al-Zamakhsharī — one of the heads and leading figures of the Muʿtazila — tried to breach the consensus and reported a reading in the nominative, with (خلقناه) in the position of the adjective and (بقدر) as the predicate, or the clause (خلقناه) as the predicate and (بقدر) a ḥāl. His wording is: "(كل شيء) is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb explained by the overt one; and it was read (كل شيء) in the nominative." Abū al-Sammāl alone read it so, and it is anomalous (shādhdha).
2- A thorough summary of the topic of ishtighāl (preoccupation): here is a thorough summary of the topic of ishtighāl.
As for its definition: it is that a noun comes first and there comes after it a fully conjugable verb, or a noun resembling one, that puts in the accusative a pronoun referring to it, or something connected with its pronoun, either through an intermediary or otherwise; and that governor is such that, were it freed from that governed word and given power over the preceding noun, it would put it in the accusative. The accusative is obligatory when the preceding noun comes after something specific to verbs, such as the particles of urging, e.g. "hallā Zaydan akramtahu" (why not honour Zayd?); the interrogative particles other than the hamza, e.g. "hal Zaydan raʾaytahu" (did you see Zayd?); and the conditional particles, e.g. "ḥaythumā Zaydan laqītahu fa-akrimhu" (wherever you meet Zayd, honour him). The accusative is preferable in six cases:
1- That the preoccupied verb is a request, namely a command or a supplication for good or ill.
2- That the preoccupied verb is joined to the lām or the lā of request, e.g. "ʿAmran li-yaḍribhu Bakr" (ʿAmr — let Bakr strike him) and "Khālidan lā tuhinhu" (Khālid — do not insult him).
3- That the noun from which [the verb] is preoccupied comes after something that is mostly followed by a verb. There are examples of this, among them the interrogative hamza, e.g. (أبشرا منّا واحدا نتبعه).
4- That the noun from which [the verb] is preoccupied comes after a conjunction not separated by "ammā" (with fatḥa on the hamza and doubled mīm), preceded by a verb not built on a noun before it, e.g. "qāma Zaydun wa-ʿAmran akramtuhu" (Zayd stood, and ʿAmr I honoured), and the words of the Exalted (والأنعام خلقها لكم); as opposed to e.g. "ḍarabtu Zaydan wa-ammā ʿAmrun fa-ahantuhu" (I struck Zayd, and as for ʿAmr, I insulted him), where the preferred is the nominative.
5- That with the nominative it might be imagined that the verb preoccupied with the pronoun is an adjective of what precedes it, e.g. (إنّا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر). For if (كل) were nominative, (خلقناه) could be its predicate, and the meaning would be the universality of the creation of existing beings by measure, whether good or evil, as is the doctrine of the Sunna; and (خلقناه) could be an adjective of (شيء) with (بقدر) the predicate of (كل). Specification by the adjective suggests that what is not described by it is not by measure; the adjective is the createdness attributed to Him, so createdness not attributed to Him would not be by measure, which suggests that there is something created by other than Him, the Exalted — and that is the doctrine of the Muʿtazila. That is not imagined with the accusative of (كل), as the object of an omitted verb explained by (خلقنا); and it is impossible to make it an adjective of (كل شيء), because the adjective does not govern the qualified noun, and what does not govern does not explain a governor. Hence the nominative of (كل) is obligatory if the verb attached to the pronoun is an adjective of (كل شيء), e.g. (وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر), i.e. the books. The accusative of (كل) is not valid here, because supposing the verb to be given power over it is only according to the intended meaning, and the meaning here is not that they did everything in the books, such that (فعلوا) could be given power over (كل شيء); rather the meaning is: everything done by them is recorded in the books, which differs from that meaning. So the nominative of (كل) is obligatory as a subject; the later verb is an adjective of it or of (شيء), and (في الزبر) is the predicate of (كل).
Moreover, Sībawayh did not consider the suggestion of an adjective a reason for preferring the accusative, as Ibn Mālik did; rather Sībawayh made the accusative the less preferred option in the verse mentioned. He said: "As for the words of the Exalted (إنّا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر), it came only after the manner of 'Zaydan ḍarabtuhu' (Zayd — I struck him), and that is good, abundant Arabic." Ibn al-Shajarī said: "The Basrans agreed regarding this verse that the nominative is preferable, since nothing precedes that requires the accusative; the Kufans said: the accusative is better in it, because a governor that puts in the accusative precedes (كل), namely (إنّ), and that called for implying (خلقنا)."
6- The sixth case in which the accusative is preferable: that the noun from which [the verb] is preoccupied is an answer to a question [whose interrogative word is] put in the accusative by what follows it, like "Zaydan ḍarabtuhu" (Zayd I struck) in answer to one who said: "Which of them did you strike?" or "Whom did you strike?" — Zayd is preferably accusative because it is an answer to the question, so that the answer matches the question as a verbal clause.
Moreover, in His words (وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر), the nominative of (كل) is obligatory and its accusative impossible, because supposing the verb to be given power over it is only according to the intended meaning, and the meaning here is not that they did everything in the books, such that (فعلوا) could be given power over (كل شيء); the later verb is an adjective of it or of (شيء).

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُزْدَجَرٌ) a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with a prefixed mīm) from الزجر (rebuke), except that the tāʾ was replaced by dāl so as to agree with the zāy in voicing; you may also take it as a noun of place, i.e. a place of admonition.
(نُكُرٍ) abhorrent and dreadful, something that souls disown because of its terror; it is the Day of Resurrection.
(مُهْطِعِينَ) الإهطاع is hurrying with outstretched necks and craning gazes, constantly, never relenting from staring; it is a living, embodied image of the terrified dread that looks toward the horrors it awaits.

* I'rab:
(اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ) اقتربت الساعة: a past verb and an agent; وانشق القمر is conjoined to the preceding clause. (وَإِنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا وَيَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; يعرضوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ويقولوا is conjoined to يعرضوا; سحر is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this"; and مستمر is an adjective of سحر. There are four views on مستمر. The first, which is the apparent one, is that it means continuous and uniform. It is also said: مستمر means strong and firmly made, from their saying "his rope was twisted firm" (استمر مريره); al-Buḥturī said, describing the wolf:
طواه الطوى حتى استمر مريره ... فما فيه إلا الروح والعظم والجلد
(Hunger folded him up until his rope was twisted taut, so that nothing is left in him but spirit, bone and skin.)
It is also said that it is from "the thing became bitter" (استمر الشيء), when its bitterness grows intense so that it cannot be swallowed; and it is said that مستمر means passing, going away, not remaining. All these possibilities are admissible. (وَكَذَّبُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ) The wāw is a conjunction; كذبوا is a verb and an agent; اتبعوا is a verb and an agent; and أهواءهم is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). The secret of the shift from the imperfect to the past will come in the section on Rhetoric. The next wāw is resumptive; وكل أمر: كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مستقر its khabar (predicate). The clause is a resumption, intended to drive despair into their hearts regarding what they used as grounds for their lying hopes. There are readings of مستقر, among them مستقر with fatḥa on the qāf, as a noun of place, a noun of time, or a mīmī maṣdar, i.e. possessing a place of settling, or a time of settling, or settling. It was also read in the genitive, as an adjective of أمر, in which case كل is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "acted upon"; or conjoined to الساعة, which Abū Ḥayyān considered unlikely because of the length of separation by three clauses. (وَلَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْباءِ ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for an oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; جاءهم is a past verb with a direct object; من الأنباء is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ما; ما is relative or indefinite (mawṣūfa), and in both cases it is the agent of جاءهم; فيه is a fronted khabar and مزدجر a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (حِكْمَةٌ بالِغَةٌ فَما تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ) حكمة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a badal (substitute) of ما; بالغة is an adjective of حكمة, and the object of بالغة is omitted, the implied form being "reaching its utmost", i.e. no flaw can find its way into it. The fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative or interrogative of denial, and it is in the position of accusative as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), i.e. "what avail do the warnings avail?"; it is also permissible to make it a fronted direct object, i.e. "what thing of all things do the warnings avail?". تغن is an imperfect verb, nominative, and النذر is the agent of تغن. (فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); تول is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "you", i.e. do not argue with them in speech. عنهم: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تول. يوم is an adverbial attached to an implied "remember", or to يخرجون. The clause يدع is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The yāʾ of يدعو was dropped in writing, and الداعي is the agent of يدعو; it was also read with the yāʾ dropped, being content with the kasra. إلى شيء: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يدعو; and نكر is an adjective of شيء. (خُشَّعاً أَبْصارُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ) خشعا is a ḥāl; it was also read خاشعة and خاشعا; and أبصارهم is the agent of خشعا. al-Zajjāj said: you may, with active participles when they precede the plural, use the singular, saying خاشعا أبصارهم; you may use the singular and feminine, as in خاشعة أبصارهم; and you may use the plural, as in خشعا أبصارهم. You say "I passed by youths with handsome faces" in all three forms: حسن أوجههم, حسنة أوجههم, and حسان وجوههم. He said:
وشباب حسن أوجههم ... من إياد بن نزار بن معبد
(And youths of handsome faces, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿbad.)
al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that in خشعا there is their pronoun and that أبصارهم is a badal (substitute) of it." The clause يخرجون is resumptive; من الأجداث: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يخرجون. كأن with its noun, and جراد is its khabar and منتشر an adjective; and the clause كأنهم جراد is a ḥāl. (مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ يَقُولُ الْكافِرُونَ هذا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ) مهطعين is accusative as a ḥāl too, from the agent of يخرجون; إلى الداع: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مهطعين. The clause يقول الكافرون is resumptive, as though it came as an answer to a question arising from the description of the Day by terrors and of its people by wretched condition, as if it were said "what will happen then?" and it was answered "the disbelievers will say". Some allowed that the clause be a ḥāl from the agent of يخرجون; so the ḥāl-phrases from the wāw would be four, one fronted and three postponed. The clause هذا يوم عسر is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole: In His saying «اقتربت الساعة» there is added intensity over "drew near" (قرب), just as in اقتدر there is added intensity over قدر, because the basis of the form افتعل is to prepare the meaning with intensity, as in اشتوى when one takes roast meat (شواء) with intensity in preparing it.
2- Shift from the imperfect to the past: In His saying, the Exalted, «وكذبوا واتبعوا أهواءهم» there is a shift from the imperfect, as the apparent context would require, since كذبوا and اتبعوا are conjoined to يعرضوا; the secret of this shift is to signal that these two are among their ancient habits.
3- The loose, detailed simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mufaṣṣal): In His saying «يخرجون من الأجداث كأنهم جراد منتشر» there is a loose, detailed simile, because all four elements are present in it; He likened them to locusts in multitude and surging. The wording of al-Qurṭubī is «كأنهم جراد منتشر مهطعين إلى الداع», and he said in another place: «يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث». "These are two descriptions at two different times. One is at the coming out from the graves: they come out terrified, not guided as to where they should head, so they enter into one another; they are then like scattered moths, some of them scattered among others, with no direction to aim at. Then when they hear the caller they head for him, and become like spread-out locusts, because locusts have a direction at which they aim." This is a fine observation. This simile gives the picture embodiment and personification: these crowds coming out of the graves, in the blink of an eye, resemble locusts, famed for their spreading and swarming without having any goal in this spreading and swarming. Likewise these crowds have been bridled by fear, their minds knotted by terror, stricken with still depths of bewilderment and covered with waves of misguidance and rust (al-rayn); so they go on, answering the call of the caller without knowing why he calls them, though they know vaguely that he calls them to something abhorrent whose reality they cannot fathom and whose import they do not know.

dervis-irab:9-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُنْهَمِرٍ) المنهمر: poured out with force and abundance. In al-Mukhtār: «همر the tears and the water: he poured it out, of the pattern naṣara; and انهمر the water: it flowed». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
راح تمريه الصبا ثم انتحى ... فيه شؤبوب جنوب منهمر
(The east wind drove it along in the evening, then a downpour of the south wind, streaming, turned toward it.)
(وَفَجَّرْنَا) التفجير is the splitting of the earth open for water. The fāʾ together with the jīm, as the first and second radicals, has a particular unusual property: the two indicate splitting and cleaving. So فجأ and فجئ: فجئا, فجأة and فجاءة; and فاجأ مفاجأة the man: he rushed upon him or came to him suddenly without his being aware of it. الفجر is the light of morning, in which there is a cleaving of the darkness of night and a splitting of its blackest depths. "So-and-so walked مفاجّا between his legs", i.e. holding them apart; and in their riddles: "What thing spreads its legs and does not urinate?" It is the table, something like a bed with four legs on which they place their goods. افتج the man: he took the broad roads; الفج (pl. فجاج and فجاج) is the wide, clear road between two mountains. "So-and-so rode a great فجرة", and he is of the people of الفجر, not of the people of الفجور; this is generosity. The torrent spread out in the مفاجر of the valley and its مرافض, the places to which the torrents are discharged. فجعه what befell him, and فجّعه. They say: "Time is one that springs evil upon one, bereaving; it gives in its giving, then takes back." الفجوة is the wide opening.
(عُيُوناً) plural of عين الماء (the spring), which is what gushes from the earth in a circle like the roundness of an animal's eye. So عين is shared between the eye of an animal, the spring of water, the substance of gold, the "eye" of the cloud, and the "eye" of the well. The عين is called a ينبوع (pl. ينابيع), and المنبع, with fatḥa on the mīm and the bāʾ, is the outlet of the water (pl. منابع).
(وَدُسُرٍ) الدسر: the nails with which the ship is fastened, its singular being دسار and دسير; "دسرت the ship, I fasten it (أدسرها دسرا)" when you fasten it. It is said that the basis of the root is pushing; one says "he دسره with the spear" if he pushed it hard. الدسر is also the ship's breast, because with it the water is pushed away; hence the hadith about ambergris: «هو شيء دسره البحر» ("it is something the sea has thrust out"). In al-Mukhtār: «الدسر: pushing, of the pattern naṣara». The two views can be reconciled, because the nail is driven into its place. More on this meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(مُدَّكِرٍ) its origin is مذتكر; the tāʾ was changed to dāl to agree with the voicing of the dhāl, then the dāl was assimilated into it.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُوا عَبْدَنا وَقالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وَازْدُجِرَ) كذبت: a past verb, the tāʾ being feminine; قبلهم: an adverb of time, accusative because of annexation, attached to كذبت; قوم نوح: the agent of كذبت. فكذبوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; كذبوا a verb and an agent; عبدنا a direct object; وقالوا is conjoined to كذبوا; مجنون is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is mad"; ازدجر may be conjoined to قالوا, i.e. they were not content with this saying but added to it rebuking and scolding him; and it is said it is conjoined to "he is mad", so it falls within the scope of what they said, i.e. they said "he is mad and the jinn have rebuked him, tossed him about and carried off his mind". ازدجر is a passive past verb. (فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فَانْتَصِرْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; دعا ربه: a past verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; أن and what is in its scope are in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "that I am overcome", reporting the meaning (had it been reporting the wording, one would say إنه مغلوب); أن with its noun and predicate; the fāʾ is a conjunction; انتصر is an imperative, i.e. "take vengeance for me on them", so what انتصر is attached to is omitted, as you see. (فَفَتَحْنا أَبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied omitted element, i.e. "so We answered Noah's prayer, so We opened"; فتحنا a verb and an agent; أبواب السماء a direct object; بماء: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to فتحنا, and the bāʾ is for transitivity with hyperbole, in that the water is made like the instrument with which one opens, as you say "I opened with the key"; it is also permissible for the bāʾ to be for accompaniment, i.e. accompanied by streaming water, in which case it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; منهمر is an adjective of ماء. (وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُوناً فَالْتَقَى الْماءُ عَلى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ) وفجرنا is conjoined to فتحنا; الأرض is a direct object; عيونا is a tamyīz (specification), for the attribution of فجرنا to الأرض is vague and عيونا clarifies this vagueness. The original is "We made the springs of the earth burst", so the muḍāf was transformed, the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place, and the muḍāf was brought as a tamyīz. فالتقى is conjoined to فجرنا; الماء is the agent of التقى; على أمر: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to التقى, and على gives the sense of cause; the meaning is "it gathered for the sake of their drowning, which had been decreed from eternity". It is also said to be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. The clause قد قدر is an adjective of أمر. (وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ أَلْواحٍ وَدُسُرٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; حملناه a verb, an agent and a direct object; على ذات: attached to حملناه; ألواح is a muḍāf ilayhi; ودسر is conjoined to ألواح. (تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنا جَزاءً لِمَنْ كانَ كُفِرَ) The clause is an adjective of ذات دسر, and ذات ألواح is originally an adjective of سفينة, so this is a second adjective. تجري is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ; بأعيننا is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in تجري, i.e. watched over and guarded by Our eyes; جزاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "We did that as a recompense", or with the implied "We recompensed them with a recompense"; it may also be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl; لمن: attached to جزاء; and the clause كان is the ṣila of من. (وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْناها آيَةً فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; تركناها a past verb, an agent and a direct object; the pronoun refers to the deed, namely their drowning in the manner mentioned, and al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it refer to the ship. آية is a ḥāl, or a second direct object if تركنا means "We made it". The fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; من is a redundant preposition; مدكر is genitive in form, nominative in position, as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "existing". (فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ) The first fāʾ is preferably the eloquent fāʾ, as if He said "if you know what befell them all as a fitting recompense for their deeds, then how was My punishment?" كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, the fronted khabar of كان; كان عذابي: كان with its noun; and نذري is conjoined to عذابي. The yāʾ is not written in the script because it is among the "extra" yāʾs (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid); the same is said of all the places to come, though it was read with the yāʾ retained. The meaning of the question will come under Rhetoric. (وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ) It is conjoined to what precedes; للذكر: attached to يسرنا; and the meaning is "We have prepared it for remembrance", from "he made his she-camel ready for travel" and "he made his horse ready for raiding" when he saddled and bridled it. He said:
وقمت إليه باللجام ميسرا ... هنالك يجزيني الذي كنت أصنع
(And I rose to it with the bridle, making it ready; there it repays me for what I used to do.)
The meaning of the verse: "I rose to it, preparing and equipping the bridle for it", or "making it easy for it with the bridle, indicating that it would have been unruly were it not for the bridle". هنالك points to the place of the war and its time; يجزيني means "gives me the recompense of my doing toward it", and he likened it to one from whom recompense is valid, by way of the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- Substitution of attributes for the things described: In His saying «وحملناه على ذات ألواح ودسر» there is a metonymy (kināya) for a thing described, namely the ship; the attributes have taken the place of the things described and performed their function, so that nothing separates them. Similar is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
مفرشي صهوة الحصان ... ولكن قميصي مسرودة من حديد
(My bedding is the horse's back, but my shirt is woven of iron.)
He meant "but my shirt is a coat of mail". In the verse, if you were to join the ship with this attribute, or the coat of mail with this attribute, it would not be sound. This is among eloquent and ingenious speech. [Translator's note: the source prints «وقله» for «وقوله»; translated as «His saying». The verse is quoted as printed.]
2- Repetition: In His saying «فهل من مدّكر» there is repetition, whose definition has already been given. We say here that the benefit of repetition is that they may renew admonition on hearing each report; and marvellous things will come from the rules of repetition.
3- The meaning of the question: In His saying «فكيف كان عذابي ونذر» the question here asks about the state, i.e. it was of a terrible manner that description cannot encompass; the meaning is to bring those addressed to acknowledge that His, the Exalted's, punishment befalls the deniers.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صَرْصَراً) الصرصر: a wind blowing so violently that its sound is heard; it is the doubled form of صر, and the repetition of letters signals repetition of the action, as has already been discussed; similarly كبّ and كبكب, نه and نهنه.
(أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ) الأعجاز: plural of عجز; the عجز of anything is its rear, and hence العجز (the buttocks), because it leads to the lagging behind of matters. نخل (palm trees) is treated as both masculine and feminine.
(مُنْقَعِرٍ) uprooted from its base, because the قعر of a thing is its bottom; hence "so-and-so تقعر in his speech" when he delved deeply into it.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ عادٌ فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ) كذبت عاد: a past verb and an agent; وكيف كان عذابي ونذر: its i'rab has already been given. (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ) إن with its noun, and the clause أرسلنا عليهم is its khabar; the clause is resumptive, intended to explain what was left general. ريحا is the direct object of أرسلنا; صرصرا is a naʿt (adjective) of ريحا; and مستمر is an adjective of النحس or of اليوم. The discussion of the "day of ill omen" will come in the section on Benefits. (تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ) The clause is an adjective of ريحا; كأن with its noun, and أعجاز نخل is its khabar; and منقعر is an adjective of نخل [Translator's note: the source prints «منعقر» here]. The clause is a ḥāl, a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated); more on this simile will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ) its i'rab has already been given. (وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ) its i'rab was given shortly before, so renew your acquaintance with it.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «تنزع الناس» the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun, to give generality, i.e. the uprooting includes males and females together; otherwise the original would be تنزعهم. Mujāhid said: "It would throw the man on his head, so his head and neck and what adjoins them of his body would be shattered." It is also said that they used to line up, holding one another's hands, and enter the ravines and dig pits and burrow into them, and the wind would pull them out and break their necks.
2- Simile: In His saying «كأنهم أعجاز نخل منقعر» there is a loose, representational simile (tashbīh mursal tamthīlī): He likened them to the trunks of uprooted palms as they fell on the ground dead, being tall, massive corpses. It is also said that the wind would cut off their heads, leaving bodies without heads, so they resembled the trunks of palms torn from where they were planted.

* Benefits:
The day of ill omen (yawm al-naḥs): al-Zajjāj said: "It is said that it was on a Wednesday at the end of the month that does not revolve." From this the ill omen became attached to the Wednesday that does not revolve. al-Shihāb said in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: "People take ill omen from the last Wednesday of every month and call it 'the Wednesday that does not revolve'; their taking ill omen from it does not require that it be ill-omened in itself." More of this discussion will come in Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa.

dervis-irab:23-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُعُرٍ) It may be a singular, i.e. madness; one says "a mad she-camel" (ناقة مسعورة), i.e. like a mad one in her going. He said:
كأنّ بها سعرا إذا العيس هزّها ... ذميل وإرخاء من السير متعب
(It is as though she had madness in her when the pale camels are stirred by a steady pace and a loosened gait, a wearying kind of going.)
He says: "It is as if my she-camel had madness, because of the strength of her going." العيس is the plural of عيساء, the white she-camels, stirred by ذميل and إرخاء, two kinds of going, each of them wearying. The attribution of the stirring to the two is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī) of the type of attribution to the cause; and if by "stirring" is meant driving, it is attribution to the maṣdar, as in "his luck was lucky" (جد جده). It may also be the plural of سعير, which is fire.
(الْأَشِرُ) one extremely given to exultant insolence and arrogance; it is thus an intensive form; it is also said to be a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), like حذر, يقظ, وطف and عجز. In al-Mukhtār: «أشر and بطر, of the pattern ṭarib or fariḥ».
(مُحْتَضَرٌ) a passive participle of احتضر in the sense of حضر, because the water was divided among them, each party having a day, i.e. each share of the water is attended by one party and no other attends with it; so on the day of the she-camel she attends it, and on their day they attend it. حضر and احتضر are one in meaning. He said "a division among them" only by giving preference to those with reason; the meaning is one day for them and one day for her.
(فَتَعاطى) so he took up the sword and hamstrung her; its derivation has already passed. [Translator's note: the source reads «وقد مرّ مدتها», as printed; the sense is taken as "its root (مادتها) has already been covered", and the source wording may be a misprint.]
(الْمُحْتَظِرِ) with kasra on the ẓāʾ, an active participle: the one who makes an enclosure (ḥaẓīra) of firewood and the like; الحظيرة is the pen. In al-Mukhtār: «The ḥaẓīra is made for camels from trees to protect them from cold and wind, and the muḥtaẓir, with kasra on the ẓāʾ, is the one who makes it». The meaning is that they became like dry, crumbled trees when shattered; الهشيم is what is broken up and crumbled.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ) A past verb and an agent; بالنذر: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كذبت. It has been said before that النذر is either a maṣdar, with the meaning of warning (al-indhār), or the plural of نذير, i.e. a warner. (فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا واحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا a past verb and an agent. In أبشرا the hamza is interrogative, and بشرا is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation), i.e. by an implied verb explained by what follows: "shall we follow a mortal?". منا is an adjective of بشرا; واحدا has two possible analyses, the clearer being that it is an adjective of بشرا, except that this is problematic as the interpreted adjective is fronted before the explicit adjective; the reply is that منا is then not an adjective but a ḥāl from واحدا, fronted before it. The second analysis is that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in نتبعه; and بشر applies to the singular and the plural. نتبعه: an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إن with its noun; إذن is a particle of answer and recompense, inoperative; لفي: the lām is the shifted lām, and في ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element which is the khabar of إن; and سعر is conjoined to ضلال. (أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ) The hamza is for a question of denial; ألقي is a passive past verb and الذكر a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʾil); عليه: attached to ألقي; من بيننا is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in عليه, i.e. singled out; بل is a particle of rejoinder and conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ, كذاب its khabar and أشر an adjective. (سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ) The clauses are the content of an omitted saying, its implied form being "Allah the Exalted said"; the sīn is for the future; يعلمون a verb and an agent; غدا an adverb attached to يعلمون; من an interrogative noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and الكذاب its khabar and الأشر an adjective; the clause is suspended (muʿallaqa) because the interrogative stands at its head, and it fills the place of the two objects of يعلمون. (إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ وَاصْطَبِرْ) إن with its noun, and مرسلو الناقة is its khabar; the clause is resumptive, to explain what was promised; فتنة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. as a test for them; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; ارتقبهم: an imperative, a latent agent and a direct object; واصطبر is conjoined to ارتقبهم, and what اصطبر is attached to is omitted, i.e. "and be patient with their harm". (وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; نبئهم: an imperative verb, a latent agent, the implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is the first object; أن and what is in its scope are in the position of the second and third objects, because نبّأ takes three objects; أن with its noun, and قسمة is its khabar; بينهم is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of قسمة (mentioned as "divided"), or to قسمة because it means "divided"; كل is a mubtadaʾ, شرب a muḍāf ilayhi, and محتضر the khabar of كل, i.e. attended by them or by the she-camel. (فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; نادوا a past verb and an agent; what it is conjoined upon is omitted, i.e. "they persisted in that"; and it is better to take it as the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. they remained so for a time, then grew weary of the drying up of the water and the barrenness of the pastures, and agreed to kill her and concurred on lying in wait for her where she passed, and Qudār ibn Sālif volunteered for this matter, whose story has been given before; so they called him and he took it up. صاحبهم is a direct object; فتعاطى is conjoined to فنادوا, i.e. he dared to take up this matter without regard for it; فعقر is conjoined to تعاطى. (فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ) its i'rab was given shortly before. (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ) إن with its noun, and the clause أرسلنا is its khabar; عليهم: attached to أرسلنا; صيحة is a direct object and واحدة an adjective; فكانوا is conjoined to أرسلنا, the wāw being the noun of كان, and الهشيم المحتظر its khabar [Translator's note: the source writes «الهشيم المحتظر»; the verse has كهشيم المحتظر]. It was also read with fatḥa (المحتظَر), as a noun of place, which is the place of enclosure-making, i.e. the ḥaẓīra. (وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ) its i'rab was given shortly before.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «سيعلمون غدا من الكذاب الأشر» there is the art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām), so that the threat is more charged with vengeance and the menace more potent in souls. He gave it in the form of vagueness although they were the ones meant, because He intended the time of death and did not intend a specific tomorrow; this is common in Arabic poetry. Abū al-Ṭammāḥ said:
ألا عللاني قبل نوح النوائح ... وقبل اضطراب النفس بين الجوانح
وقبل غد يا لهف نفسي في غد ... إذا راح أصحابي ولست برائح
(Distract me before the wailing of the mourning women, and before the soul convulses between the ribs; and before tomorrow, alas for my soul on that tomorrow, when my companions depart and I do not depart.)
He meant the time of death and did not intend a specific tomorrow. Of this too is the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
للموت فيها سهام غير مخطئة ... من لم يكن ميتا في اليوم مات غدا
(Death has arrows in it that do not miss; whoever does not die today dies tomorrow.)
2- Simile: In His saying «فكانوا كهشيم المحتظر» there is a loose simile (tashbīh mursal) for their destruction and annihilation.
